paragraphs: Dior Maison unveils new designs for the Lily of the Valley collection with a subtle homage to the founding couturier's lucky flower. Inspired by the eponymous dress created by Mr. Dior for the Spring-Summer 1957 Haute Couture Fashion Show, delicate, embossed bell-shaped flowers accent a set of sophisticated creations, including glasses, candles and even table linens. Continuing this pastoral poetry, a selection of glassware pieces is enhanced by four-leaf clovers or engraved with lilies of the valley, in a bucolic ode to Christian Dior's passion for superstition. As a final surprise, elegant palm tree and ladybug ceramic candle holders, available in green and white, complete this exceptional selection. The refined collection suggests a springtime getaway and sunny days to come. *These objects of desire were developed in collaboration with the Jean Roger workshop.
bullets: Lily of the Valley, White and Green

paragraphs: Having inherited a passion for flowers from my mother, I especially enjoyed the company of plants and gardeners, Christian Dior confided in his memoirs. Adorned with designs of lily of the valley, the couturier's lucky charm, the Lily of the Valley tableware line is enhanced by new wicker pieces — like placemats, baskets, frames and boxes — decorated with sprigs of the flower.
